### Links

This script takes one or more alignment files in SAM/BAM format and a feature file in GFF format and calculates for each feature the number of reads mapping to it. 

See http://htseq.readthedocs.io/en/master/count.html for details.


::: {.ref-description}
This script takes one or more alignment files in SAM/BAM format and a feature file in GFF format and calculates for each feature the number of reads mapping to it.

See http://htseq.readthedocs.io/en/master/count.html for details.
:::

::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}

:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--order`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Sorting order of <alignment_file>. Paired-end sequencing data must be sorted either by position or
by read name, and the sorting order must be specified. Ignored for single-end data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"name"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"pos"`, `"name"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--stranded`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether the data is from a strand-specific assay. 'reverse' means 'yes' with reversed strand interpretation.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"yes"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"reverse"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--minimum_alignment_quality`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Skip all reads with MAPQ alignment quality lower than the given minimum value.
MAPQ is the 5th column of a SAM/BAM file and its usage depends on the software
used to map the reads.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `10`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--type`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Feature type (3rd column in GTF file) to be used, all features of other type are ignored (default, suitable for Ensembl GTF files: exon)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"exon"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--id_attribute`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
GTF attribute to be used as feature ID (default, suitable for Ensembl GTF files: gene_id).
All feature of the right type (see -t option) within the same GTF attribute will be added
together. The typical way of using this option is to count all exonic reads from each gene
and add the exons but other uses are possible as well. You can call this option multiple
times: in that case, the combination of all attributes separated by colons (:) will be used
as a unique identifier, e.g. for exons you might use -i gene_id -i exon_number.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"gene_id"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--additional_attributes`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Additional feature attributes (suitable for Ensembl GTF files: gene_name). Use multiple times
for more than one additional attribute. These attributes are only used as annotations in the
output, while the determination of how the counts are added together is done based on option -i.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"gene_name"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--add_chromosome_info`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Store information about the chromosome of each feature as an additional attribute
(e.g. colunm in the TSV output file).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--mode`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Mode to handle reads overlapping more than one feature.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"union"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"union"`, `"intersection-strict"`, `"intersection-nonempty"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--non_unique`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether and how to score reads that are not uniquely aligned or ambiguously assigned to features.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"none"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"none"`, `"all"`, `"fraction"`, `"random"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--secondary_alignments`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to score secondary alignments (0x100 flag).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"score"`, `"ignore"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--supplementary_alignments`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to score supplementary alignments (0x800 flag).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"score"`, `"ignore"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--counts_output_sparse`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Store the counts as a sparse matrix (mtx, h5ad, loom).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_true`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/mapping/htseq_count/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/mapping/htseq_count);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/mapping/htseq_count/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
